title: The case of Phineas Gage: overview (R-10024)
description: The case of Phineas Gage is a historical case of the nervous system. First described in 1848. Its role: an 1848 railroad accident drove an iron rod through his frontal lobe, changing his personality and revealing the lobe’s role. Key fact: a landmark case in neuropsychology. Closely associated with frontal lobe, personality, and case study.
